atoms.a: Canada is a large country in North America where English and French are the official languages. It is famous for its beautiful nature, with forests, lakes, and mountains. Canada is also a multicultural country with people from many different backgrounds and modern cities.

You might think of Canada as an English-speaking country but did you know that it has a second commonly spoken language? That's right, some Canadians are French-speakers. Quebec in the east of the country is the only region in North America with a French-speaking majority, as well as one of only two provinces in Canada where French is a constitutionally recognized official language.
Last time the population was asked, 79% of all residents of Quebec listed French as their mother tongue. Since it is the official language in the province, around 95% of all citizens speak French.
b: ++French is the mother tongue of 79% of residents of Quebec.
++French is the official language in Quebec.

instruction.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f2Poly'> There is an English and a French way of spelling Kebeck. Its biggest city is Montreal, though its capital is Quebec City. The Province's motto is <voice voiceLang='fr' voice='f2Poly'>Je me souviens </voice>in French, which translates to: I remember. A very popular dish that is said to have originated in Quebec is <voice voiceLang='fr' voice='f2Poly'>Poutine,</voice>, made of French Fries, gravy and cheese curds. Overall, French is truly at the heart of Quebec's identity.</voice>
